title: First seal: a rider on a white horse goes out conquering
summary: The Lamb opens the first seal and a rider with a bow and a crown goes out conquering. Constable thinks the rider is most probably the Antichrist, who makes a covenant with Israel; placed at the start of the seven years (Johnson #389–390).

sources.name: Thomas Constable, Expository Notes on Revelation 6

title: Second seal: a red horse takes peace from the earth
summary: A rider on a red horse is given a great sword to take peace from the earth so that men kill one another. Constable places the seals in the first half of the Tribulation and links this warfare to Gog and Magog (Ezekiel 38–39).

sources.name: Thomas Constable, Expository Notes on Revelation 6

title: Third seal: black horse and famine prices; oil and wine spared
summary: A rider on a black horse holds scales: a measure of wheat for a day's wage, while oil and wine are not to be hurt. Constable reads it as famine and control of commodity prices in the first half of the Tribulation.

sources.name: Thomas Constable, Expository Notes on Revelation 6

title: Fifth seal: martyrs under the altar cry "How long?"
summary: The souls of those slain for the word of God cry for vengeance, are given white robes, and are told to wait until their fellow servants are also killed. Constable takes them as Tribulation believers martyred after the Rapture.

sources.name: Thomas Constable, Expository Notes on Revelation 6

title: Seventh seal: silence in heaven, then seven trumpets given
summary: The seventh seal brings silence in heaven for about half an hour; seven angels receive trumpets and fire from the altar is cast to the earth with thunder and an earthquake. It opens the trumpet judgments, after the sixth seal's start of the wrath (Johnson #462–463).

title: First trumpet: hail and fire mixed with blood burn a third of trees
summary: Hail and fire mingled with blood fall on the earth; a third of the trees and all green grass are burnt up. Part of the wrath that Johnson begins at the sixth seal (#463).

title: Second trumpet: a burning mountain cast into the sea
summary: Something like a great burning mountain is cast into the sea; a third of the sea becomes blood, a third of sea life dies and a third of ships are destroyed.

title: Third trumpet: the star Wormwood makes a third of the waters bitter
summary: A great star burning like a lamp, named Wormwood, falls on a third of the rivers and springs; the waters turn bitter and many die.

title: Fourth trumpet: a third of sun, moon and stars darkened
summary: A third of the sun, moon and stars is struck so that a third of the day and night have no light. An eagle then announces three woes for the last three trumpets.

title: Fifth trumpet: locusts from the bottomless pit torment men five months
summary: A fallen star opens the bottomless pit; locust-like creatures under Abaddon/Apollyon torment for five months those without God's seal, so that men seek death and cannot find it (the first woe).

title: Sixth trumpet: four angels loosed at the Euphrates; a third of mankind killed
summary: Four angels bound at the Euphrates are released with an army of 200 million horsemen, and fire, smoke and brimstone kill a third of mankind; the survivors still do not repent (the second woe).

title: Seventh trumpet: the kingdoms of this world become Christ's
summary: Loud voices announce that the kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of the Lord and of his Christ; the time of the dead to be judged has come and the ark of his testament is seen in the heavenly temple. Walvoord suggests the seven bowls are contained within this trumpet.

sources.name: John Walvoord, Revelation 11: The Two Witnesses and the Seventh Trumpet

title: First bowl: sores on those with the mark of the beast
summary: A noisome and grievous sore falls on those who have the mark of the beast and worship his image. The bowls fill up the wrath that Johnson ends at Revelation 15:1 (#465).

title: Second bowl: the sea becomes blood and every living soul in it dies
summary: The sea becomes as the blood of a dead man and every living thing in the sea dies (a third under the second trumpet; now all).

title: Third bowl: rivers and springs become blood
summary: Rivers and fountains of water become blood; the angel of the waters says it is just, because they shed the blood of saints and prophets.

title: Fourth bowl: the sun scorches men with fire
summary: Power is given to the sun to scorch men with great heat; they blaspheme God and do not repent.

title: Fifth bowl: darkness on the throne and kingdom of the beast
summary: The beast's kingdom is filled with darkness and men gnaw their tongues for pain, yet still do not repent.

title: Sixth bowl: Euphrates dried for the kings of the east
summary: The Euphrates is dried up to prepare the way of the kings of the east, and three unclean spirits like frogs from the dragon, beast and false prophet gather the kings of the whole world to Armageddon. The battle itself is Johnson #473.

title: Seventh bowl: "It is done": greatest earthquake and hundred-pound hail
summary: A voice from the throne says "It is done"; the greatest earthquake splits the great city into three parts, the cities of the nations fall, islands and mountains vanish, great Babylon is remembered, and hail of about a talent each falls.

title: The Lamb takes the seven-sealed scroll from the throne
summary: Only the slain Lamb, the Lion of Judah, is worthy to take the sealed scroll and open its seals; the elders and all creation worship him. It is the heavenly scene that begins the seal judgments, after the Rapture in pre-tribulation teaching.

title: A great multitude from every nation comes out of the great tribulation
summary: After the 144,000 are sealed, John sees a multitude no one can number, from all nations, in white robes before the throne: those who come out of the great tribulation. Usually read as Tribulation believers and martyrs.

title: The mighty angel swears there will be delay no longer
summary: A mighty angel with a little open book stands on sea and land; seven thunders speak but are sealed, and he swears that there will be no more delay: at the seventh trumpet the mystery of God will be finished.

title: The two witnesses are killed, lie in the street 3½ days, then rise
summary: When their 1,260 days of testimony end, the beast from the abyss kills the two witnesses in Jerusalem; the world rejoices over their bodies for 3½ days, then they rise and ascend in a cloud, and an earthquake kills 7,000. Johnson's #394 puts Elijah's preaching in the first half, which brings their death to the midpoint; Walvoord takes the events literally.

sources.name: John Walvoord, Revelation 11: The Two Witnesses and the Seventh Trumpet

title: War in heaven: Michael casts Satan down to the earth
summary: Michael and his angels fight the dragon, who is cast down to the earth with his angels, "having great wrath, because he knoweth that he hath but a short time"; Daniel 12:1 has Michael stand up at the time of trouble. It sets off the persecution of the woman (Johnson #459, #461).

title: The beast's deadly wound is healed and the world wonders after him
summary: One of the beast's heads is wounded to death, the deadly wound is healed, and all the world wonders after the beast and worships the dragon. Compare Johnson #400 (Zechariah 11:17: his right eye and arm damaged).

title: Three angels: everlasting gospel, Babylon is fallen, warning against the mark
summary: One angel preaches the everlasting gospel to every nation, a second announces that Babylon is fallen, and a third warns that whoever takes the mark of the beast will drink the wine of God's wrath.

title: The winepress of wrath: Messiah comes from Edom and Bozrah
summary: The Son of Man reaps the earth, and the vine of the earth is cast into the great winepress of God's wrath; blood flows to the horses' bridles for 1,600 furlongs. Isaiah sees him coming from Bozrah with garments dyed red, treading the winepress alone. Linked to Armageddon (Johnson #473) and the refuge at Petra/Bozrah (#461).

title: The ten kings and the beast turn on the harlot and burn her
summary: The ten horns and the beast hate the whore, make her desolate and naked, eat her flesh and burn her with fire, for God put it in their hearts. Walvoord places this about the midpoint, when the beast sets up his own worship, and separates it from the later fall of Babylon in Revelation 18 (existing babylon-the-great-falls).

sources.name: John Walvoord, Revelation 17: The Destruction of Ecclesiastical Babylon

title: The devil cast into the lake of fire with the beast and false prophet
summary: After the final rebellion is consumed by fire from heaven, the devil is cast into the lake of fire and brimstone where the beast and false prophet are, to be tormented day and night for ever. It follows Johnson #484 and comes before the Great White Throne.

title: The holy city, New Jerusalem, comes down from God out of heaven
summary: John sees New Jerusalem descend as a bride, 12,000 furlongs in length, breadth and height, with twelve gates named for Israel's tribes and twelve foundations for the apostles, no temple and no need of sun, for God and the Lamb are its light. It follows the new heaven and earth (Johnson #485).

title: River of the water of life and the tree of life; no more curse
summary: A pure river of the water of life flows from the throne of God and the Lamb, the tree of life bears twelve fruits with leaves for the healing of the nations, there is no more curse, and his servants see his face. It is distinct from Ezekiel's millennial river (millennial-temple).

title: Angels gather the elect from the four winds with a great trumpet
summary: After the tribulation, when the Son of Man comes, he sends his angels with a great sound of a trumpet to gather his elect from the four winds; Isaiah has a great trumpet blown and the outcasts of Israel come to worship in Jerusalem. Johnson ties the Second Coming to the Great Trump (see apr-469).

title: As in the days of Noah and Lot, so will the Son of Man's coming be
summary: People will be eating, drinking, marrying, buying and building, unaware, as before the Flood and the fall of Sodom, until the day the Son of Man is revealed. It describes the state of the world before his coming.

title: "Peace and safety", then sudden destruction: the Day of the Lord
summary: The Day of the Lord comes as a thief in the night: when they say "Peace and safety", sudden destruction comes on them as travail on a woman with child, and they will not escape. Often linked to the false peace of the covenant that begins Daniel's 70th week (Johnson #390).

title: Judgment seat of Christ (Bema): believers' works tested and rewarded
summary: Every believer will appear before the judgment seat of Christ to receive for what was done in the body; works of gold, silver and precious stones survive the fire and are rewarded, wood, hay and stubble burn, though the person is saved. Pre-tribulation teachers place it in heaven after the Rapture and before the marriage supper of the Lamb.

title: Christ hands the kingdom to the Father after all enemies are subdued
summary: Then comes the end, when Christ delivers the kingdom to God the Father, having put down all rule, authority and power; he reigns until all enemies are under his feet, and then the Son himself is subject, that God may be all in all. Premillennial teachers place it at the close of the thousand years.

title: Elam scattered to the four winds; God sets his throne in Elam
summary: God will break the bow of Elam, the chief of its might, scatter its people to all winds, destroy its king and princes and set his throne there, then restore Elam "in the latter days". Bill Salus reads it as a future, possibly nuclear, disaster in western Iran with refugees scattered worldwide, and treats it as distinct from Persia's part in Ezekiel 38.

sources.name: Bill Salus, "Iran's prophesied disaster, regime change and dispersion" (article excerpt)
Bill Salus, Nuclear Showdown in Iran: Revealing the Ancient Prophecy of Elam (2014)

title: Israel burns Gog's weapons seven years and buries the dead seven months
summary: After Gog's defeat, Israel burns the invaders' weapons for fuel for seven years and spends seven months burying the dead in the valley of Hamon-gog, and a city is named Hamonah. It follows Johnson's Gog-Magog war (#367), which he places before the ten nations rise (#368).

title: A highway from Egypt to Assyria: Egypt, Assyria and Israel blessed together
summary: In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria, the two will worship together, and Israel will be third with them, "a blessing in the midst of the land": "Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance."

title: A cloud by day and fire by night over Mount Zion
summary: When the Lord has washed away Zion's filth, the Branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious, and over every dwelling of Mount Zion he will create a cloud and smoke by day and a flaming fire by night, a canopy and shelter.

title: The earth emptied and reeling like a drunkard; few men left
summary: The LORD makes the earth empty and turns it upside down; its inhabitants are burned and few men are left, and the earth reels to and fro like a drunkard. Isaiah 24–27 is commonly read as the Day of the Lord at the end of the age.

title: Idols and false prophets cut off from the land
summary: In that day a fountain is opened for sin, the names of the idols are cut off, and the false prophets and the unclean spirit are made to pass out of the land; a would-be prophet is ashamed of his vision.

title: Plague on the armies that fought Jerusalem: flesh consumed as they stand
summary: The LORD strikes all who fought against Jerusalem: their flesh, eyes and tongues consume away while they stand, a great panic sets each against his neighbour, and the wealth of the nations is gathered. Part of the Lord's battle at his return (Johnson #470, #473).

title: One unique day, known to the LORD: at evening time it will be light
summary: On the day the LORD's feet stand on the Mount of Olives the light will not be clear or dark; it will be one day known to the LORD, neither day nor night, but at evening time it will be light.

title: The land becomes a plain and Jerusalem is lifted up
summary: All the land from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem is turned into a plain, Jerusalem is lifted up and inhabited in its place, and "there shall be no more utter destruction". It goes with the splitting of the Mount of Olives (Johnson #471).
